theater: 定州、曲陽嘉山與唐河一線

battle.name: 定州之戰
battle.theater: 定州、曲陽嘉山與唐河一線
battle.brief: 後唐天成三年（928）四月，義武節度使王都在定州舉兵反唐，明宗命北面行營討使王晏球率軍討伐。五月、七月契丹兩度派騎兵解定州之圍，唐軍在曲陽嘉山與唐河大破之，圍城近十月，翌年二月城破，王都自焚。卡面羅馬標槍早隨羅馬解體絕跡，此役前排破盾之器是同類的唐制標槍與突槊。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍幹中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 定州之戰發生於後唐天成三年（928）四月至天成四年（929）二月，本質是唐室中央與河北義武軍節度使王都之間的一場藩鎮平叛戰爭，契丹（遼）以出兵相助的方式介入其中。叛方是據守定州（治安喜縣，今河北定州市西南）的義武節度使王都，以及定州城內的州兵與牙兵，領導權集中於節度使一人，屬典型的藩鎮割據體系：節度使兼領軍籍、財賦與營田，朝廷的詔令往往要經節度使衙門才生效。朝廷一方由明宗李嗣源下詔，除免王都官爵、削其節度使職銜，並進而公告天下其叛逆之罪；隨後組建北面行營，以北面行營討使王晏球總領行軍、權知定州行軍州事，副招討使兼諸道馬軍都指揮使、由橫海節度使安審通充任，鄭州防禦使張虔釗任都監。行營麾下包括禁軍精騎龍武左軍與龍武右軍，以及各道調發的州兵、團練與鄉兵，糧秣由河東與真定方向沿太行山東麓北運。契丹方面由皇帝耶律德光直接下令，先遣將領禿餒率五千騎入塞，後遣惕隱率七千騎解圍，目的是接應王都、牽制唐軍於河北，同時維持契丹在燕雲故地一帶的邊境既得利益與南下通道。
countriesEn: The War of Dingzhou was fought from the fourth month of 928 to the second month of 929 under the Later Tang, and it pitted the imperial court against Wang Du, military governor (jiedushi) of Yiwu, who held Dingzhou, with the Khitan state of Liao entering the war as an armed supporter of the rebels. The rebel side was the garrison of Dingzhou itself — the seat of the prefecture was Anxixian, a site lying southwest of present-day Dingzhou in Hebei — together with the prefectural troops and the elite soldiers of the city. Command was concentrated in the hands of the jiedushi, the classic pattern of a Hebei military governorship that had drifted toward independence: the jiedushi held the troop registers, the revenues and the garrison farms, and imperial edicts normally took effect only after passing through his office. The court side, under Emperor Mingzong Li Siyuan, issued an edict stripping Wang Du of his rank and titles and proclaimed his rebellion to the empire. A northern field camp was then raised: Wang Yanqiu was named commander of the northern camp and acting military governor of Dingzhou; An Shentong, jiedushi of Henghai and deputy commander with charge of the cavalry commands of the several circuits, and Zhang Qianzhao, defence commander of Zhengzhou, served as deputy commander and as overseer respectively. Under them served picked imperial cavalry such as the Dragon Guards left and right armies, together with prefectural troops, militia and local levies dispatched from the circuits, while the grain and provisions were carried north from Hedong and Zhending along the eastern foot of the Taihang range. On the Khitan side the order came from the emperor himself, Yelü Deguang: first the general Tu Nei with five thousand riders, and later the officer Tiyin with seven thousand horse, the object being to relieve Dingzhou, to pin the Tang army in Hebei and to hold the Khitan position on the old Yan-Yun frontier with its road southward.
people: 北面行營討使王晏球是此役的實際主導者。他到軍後不急於強攻，認為定州城堅、兵力集中，應先取關城、斷絕糧道，再坐困其糧；四月二十七日攻克北關城後，他又在西關一線築城設守，把行營的營柵與糧車線一併收進工事之中。契丹第一支援軍到時，他一度退到曲陽，在嘉山列陣迎戰，命符彥卿率龍武左軍當左翼、高行周率龍武右軍當右翼，兩翼奮戰才把契丹與叛軍的合兵擊退。七月他分兵於唐河迎擊第二支援軍，追出四十里至易州。十月明宗遣人督戰，要求強攻，他仍堅持圍而不攻，以疲叛軍，與朝廷的急躁形成對照。義武節度使王都是叛軍首領，據定州以驕拒詔，先求援於契丹，後城破自焚；契丹將領禿餒與惕隱先後率兵入塞解圍，終未能把定州守住。副招討使安審通以馬軍都指揮使身份參贊機務，鄭州防禦使張虔釗任都監，六月強攻定州時遭叛軍反擊，唐軍死傷三千餘人。定州指揮使馬讓能在最後關頭開城門引唐軍入城，成為決定勝負的一手。
peopleEn: Wang Yanqiu, commander of the northern field camp, was the man who really directed this campaign. On reaching the theatre he did not press an assault at once: he judged that Dingzhou was strongly built and that the rebels were concentrated inside it, so the right course was to seize the barrier forts, cut the supply line and then sit and wait for their grain to run out. On the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month he took the northern barrier fort, and along the western barrier line he then built a fort of his own, drawing the camp's palisades and the baggage road inside the works. When the first Khitan relief force arrived he gave ground to Quyang and deployed at Jiashan, ordering Fu Yanqing with the left army of the Dragon Guards to take the left wing and Gao Xingzhou with the right army of the Dragon Guards the right wing; only after both wings had fought hard did the Tang line throw back the combined rebel and Khitan host. In the seventh month he split off part of his force to meet the second relief army on the Tang river, pursuing it forty li to Yizhou. In the tenth month the emperor sent men to urge him to assault the city; he still insisted on surrounding rather than storming, wearing the rebels down, in sharp contrast to the court's impatience. Wang Du, military governor of Yiwu, headed the rebellion: he held Dingzhou in defiance of the court, appealed to the Khitan for help, and finally burned himself to death when the city fell. The Khitan commanders Tu Nei and Tiyin brought troops into the field in turn to relieve the city and could not hold it in the end. The deputy commander An Shentong, who also carried the charge of the cavalry commands, assisted with the operation, while Zhang Qianzhao, defence commander of Zhengzhou, served as overseer; in the sixth month he forced an assault on Dingzhou, was thrown back by the rebels' counter-stroke, and more than three thousand Tang soldiers were lost. Ma Rangneng, the Dingzhou command officer, opened the gates in the final moment and let the Tang army in, the single decisive hand on the scales.
kits: 卡面所繪的羅馬標槍，是西元前一世紀羅馬重裝步兵的標誌性短投槍：半米左右的槍身，中空而輕的槍幹前端安裝細長加重的銅質槍頭，用途是捅穿敵軍的盾牌；槍頭穿盾之後槍身折斷，敵兵只能帶著半截槍退回掩體，連盾一起帶走都很難。這種「一次性破盾投槍」在西元前的地中海世界隨羅馬軍團的編制而普及，並沿絲路上的器物流轉把同一套設計觀念帶到東亞，落到唐人兵器譜中的標槍一門——一種以標配重、講究投射與破面而非穿刺殺傷的短槍。須說明的是，928年的定州城下並沒有羅馬兵團，卡面武器在此役並非實配；它代表的是這一族「加重短投槍」在戰陣上的功能位置：由前排步卒用它在盾牆或密集隊形前撕開缺口，逼敵丟盾後退。實際作戰的是唐軍的標槍、突槊與長矛，後世《武經總要》所載唐制兵器中即有標槊、突槊一類，近身格鬥靠橫刀與環首刀，防護用皮甲與札甲，遠射靠弓弩，重弩如神臂弓、床子弩一類用於壓制城頭目標。攻城則備撞車、飛石、雲梯與被稱為「梟子機」的投石機，圍城所需則靠大批糧車與轉輸隊伍，糧道自河東、真定方向沿太行東麓通往定州。契丹一方是純粹的騎兵部隊，配角弓以作騎射游鬥，配短槍與骨朵作近身格鬥，披輕甲而不備攻城器械，所以他們只能解圍、不能久攻。
kitsEn: The weapon drawn on the card is the Roman pilum, the signature short throwing javelin of the heavy infantry of the first century BC. Its shaft is about half a metre long, hollow and light, and carries at the front a long, weighted bronze head whose purpose is to punch through an enemy shield; and because the shaft snaps off once the head has gone through the shield, the man on the receiving end can only retreat to his cover with half a javelin still in his hand, hardly able to carry his shield off with him. This one-shot shield-breaking javelin spread with the organisation of the Roman legions across the Mediterranean world of the first millennium BC, and the same design idea travelled east along the Silk Road, settling in the Chinese armory as the biaoqiang, a short spear judged by its weight and by its work of breaking a face rather than by its killing power. It must be said plainly that there was no Roman legion under the walls of Dingzhou in 928, and the weapon on the card was not present in this battle; what it stands for is the functional place of this family of weighted short javelins on the field, thrown by the front rank of foot to tear open a shield wall or a close formation and force the enemy to drop his shields and give ground. What actually fought at Dingzhou were Tang marksmen's javelins, tuzhuang short lances and long spears; the Tang armory later described in the Wujing Zongyao lists biaoliao and tuzhuang of just this type. Close fighting was done with hengdao and ring-pommel sabres, protection with leather and lamellar armour, and long-range work with bows and crossbows, heavy pieces such as the shenfu crossbow and the bed-crossbow being used to shoot down the defenders on the wall. For the siege the army brought battering rams, stone-throwers, scaling ladders and the traction trebuchets called xiaozi ji, while the blockade depended on great numbers of grain carts and transport columns whose road ran from Hedong and Zhending along the eastern foot of the Taihang to Dingzhou. The Khitan on the other side were cavalry in pure and simple: horn bows for shooting and skirmishing from the saddle, short spears and bone clubs for the work at close quarters, light armour, and no siege engines at all, which is why they could relieve the city but never take it.
tactics: 唐軍的戰術主線是「先取關城、再斷糧道、最後困斃」，而不是一開始就強攻城頭。四月二十七日王晏球乘定州叛軍初起、內部未固，先拔北關城，把戰線推到城下；五月奪西關城後，他沒有立刻展開攻城，而是以兩座關城為據，築城自守，切斷從真定、河東方向入定州的糧道，等叛軍自己耗盡。六月部將張虔釗急于求成，強行登城，結果遭守軍從城頭反擊，唐軍死傷三千餘人；此後全軍改守營柵、斷糧、環巡，避免再蹈覆轍。七月契丹惕隱率七千騎來援，王晏球分兵據唐河一線，等騎兵進入河谷狹道才出擊，擊潰之後一路追到易州，奪其輜重與馬匹。契丹騎兵的戰法是典型的遊牧式騎射：不硬攻堅城、不排密集方陣，先以兩翼掠陣、繞射騷擾，再在叛軍配合下衝擊唐軍側翼，五月那一戰正是靠這種「騎兵加城兵」的合力一度壓得唐軍退到曲陽。圍城數月後，叛軍糧盡，王都與禿餒企圖突圍未能成功，最後由定州指揮使馬讓能開門迎唐軍入城，王都在亂軍之中自焚。
tacticsEn: The spine of the Tang operation was to take the barrier forts first, cut the supply road second, and let the enemy starve third, rather than to assault the wall at the outset. On the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month, while the Dingzhou garrison had only just risen in revolt and was not yet firmly organised, Wang Yanqiu took the northern barrier fort and pushed the line up to the city. After the western barrier fell in the fifth month he did not proceed to storm the walls; instead he used the two barrier forts as his anchor, built his own fortified camp, and cut the grain road that fed Dingzhou from Zhending and Hedong, waiting for the rebels to consume what they had. In the sixth month Zhang Qianzhao, in a hurry for results, forced a direct assault; the garrison struck back from the wall and more than three thousand Tang soldiers were lost, after which the whole army stood to its camp, kept the road closed and patrolled in a ring rather than repeating the mistake. In the seventh month, when the Khitan commander Tiyin came up with seven thousand riders, Wang Yanqiu split off part of his force to hold the line along the Tang river, let the cavalry enter the narrow valley, and struck only then; the routing was followed by a pursuit all the way to Yizhou, taking wagons and horses. The Khitan method was the classic steppe pattern of mounted archery: they did not throw themselves against a strong city or form a dense line, but swept with both wings, shot from range to disturb the enemy, and only then charged a flank together with the garrison — which is exactly how the rebels and the Khitan pushed the Tang army back to Quyang in the fifth month. After months of blockade the rebels' grain ran out; the attempt by Wang Du and Tu Nei to break out failed, and in the end Ma Rangneng, the Dingzhou command officer, opened the gates to the Tang troops. Wang Du burned himself to death amid the fighting in the city.
data: 兵力方面，契丹兩次入塞的數目有明確記載：五月禿餒率五千騎，七月十九日惕隱率七千騎，兩次合計約一萬二千騎。朝廷行營的總兵力沒有留下可靠數字，史料只記其指揮序列為王晏球、安審通、張虔釗三人，麾下有龍武左軍、龍武右軍等禁軍精騎與各道州兵、團練，故此處不作推算。損失方面，嘉山一戰斬殺叛軍與契丹軍數千人；六月強攻定州，唐軍死傷三千餘人，是此役唯一明確記載的唐軍損失數字；唐河之戰後追出四十里至易州，俘獲甚眾，但確數未載；翌年二月城破，俘禿餒及二千契丹人。時間上，戰事自928年四月王都起兵，至929年二月十三日城破，前後約十個月，其中圍城階段自928年下半年延至929年正月，叛軍於正月城中糧盡。地理上，戰線自定州向北推至曲陽，在曲陽以東的嘉山列陣，後又在定州西北的唐河一線作戰，追擊最遠至易州；唐河至易州的追擊距離明確記為四十里，約二十餘公里。
dataEn: On numbers of men, the Khitan interventions are recorded exactly: five thousand riders under Tu Nei in the fifth month, and seven thousand under Tiyin on the nineteenth day of the seventh month, some twelve thousand horse in the two relief expeditions combined. No reliable figure survives for the total strength of the imperial field camp; the records name only its commanders, Wang Yanqiu, An Shentong and Zhang Qianzhao, together with picked cavalry of the Dragon Guards left and right armies and prefectural and militia troops from the circuits, so no estimate is offered here. On losses, several thousand rebels and Khitan were killed at Jiashan; the forced assault of Dingzhou in the sixth month cost the Tang army more than three thousand men, the only clearly recorded Tang casualty figure of the whole campaign; the pursuit after the Tang river fighting ran forty li to Yizhou and took many prisoners, but the exact count is not given; and when the city fell in the second month of the following year, Tu Nei and two thousand Khitan were taken alive. In time, the business ran from Wang Du's rising in the fourth month of 928 to the fall of the city on the thirteenth day of the second month of 929, about ten months in all, of which the blockade covered the second half of 928 through the first month of 929, the rebels' grain running out in that first month. In geography, the line of operations ran from Dingzhou north to Quyang, where the army deployed at Jiashan east of the city, and then to the Tang river northwest of Dingzhou, the furthest pursuit reaching Yizhou; the distance of that last pursuit is given as forty li, a little over twenty kilometres.
cause: 定州之戰的起因，是後唐中央與河北藩鎮之間長期的權力緊張在928年集中爆發。定州義武軍地處太行東麓、與河東集團接壤，是河北與太原之間的關鍵位置；其節度使自唐末以來握有重兵、常自行署置官吏、截留財賦，中央詔令在此往往需要節度使配合才落得實。節度使王都又是與河東晉王一系有瓜葛的藩鎮人物，朝廷在明宗即位、重新整頓節度使任命的同時把他的權力削弱，等於逼他表態。與此同時，契丹皇帝耶律德光即位未久，志在南下，河北一旦有事他必伸手，於是王都把求援契丹當作底牌，以為只要拖住唐軍、待北方出兵，河北的割據局面便可延續。戰爭因此不是偶發的叛亂，而是中央整頓、藩鎮自保、契丹南進三股力量在定州一點上碰撞的結果；它也延續了河北自唐末以來「藩鎮兵強財豐、拒詔成風」的積弊，衝突的導火線雖小，背後的結構卻相當硬。
causeEn: The immediate spark of the War of Dingzhou was the concentration of a long-running tension between the Later Tang court and the Hebei military governorships in 928. The Yiwu army at Dingzhou sat on the eastern foot of the Taihang range, hard against the Hedong group, holding the key position between Hebei and Taiyuan. Its jiedushi had for years held heavy troops, appointed their own officials and withheld revenues, so that imperial orders in that district generally took effect only if the governor chose to enforce them. Wang Du himself belonged to the Hebei establishment that was bound by ties to the Jin prince's party in Hedong, and when the new emperor Mingzong began reshuffling the military governorships and curtailed his authority he was effectively being summoned to give an account of himself. At the same time the Khitan emperor Yelü Deguang, only recently on the throne, was bent on expansion to the south, and if trouble broke out in Hebei he would reach out; Wang Du therefore counted on Khitan aid as his trump card, expecting that as long as the Tang army was held off and the north sent in help, the semi-independent order in Hebei could be prolonged. The war was therefore no accidental mutiny, but the collision at Dingzhou of three forces: centralising the court, self-preservation by the governors, and the southward pressure of the Khitan. The fuse was small; the structure behind it was hard.
impact: 定州之戰的直接後果，是義武軍這一支河北藩鎮的割據被壓回中央控制之下，王都自焚、契丹兵被俘，定州重歸朝廷節度使之下的州鎮體系，節度使的任命與兵籍從此更受中央控制，河北各鎮短期內不敢再明目張膽地抗詔。更深一層看，這場戰爭並沒有解決藩鎮問題的根源：州兵、牙兵與營田仍然歸節度使掌握，河北依然是唐室最難駕馭的一帶，這一格局最終在936年石敬瑭割讓燕雲、請契丹南下時暴露無遺，說明928年平定定州只是壓制而非根除。對契丹而言，兩次入塞折損數千騎、二千騎被俘，等於用實際代價換來一次沒有結果的救援，遼太宗耶律德光南下的腳步因此更為謹慎，短期內把重心放回國內整頓，這也改變了此後十年間北方兩大政權的對峙節奏。對唐軍戰術而言，「城堅則圍、以糧困敵」在王晏球手上的一次完整實踐，也成為五代宋初攻城戰中被反覆提及的範例，與後來宋人對河北城池攻守的討論常被並列。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the War of Dingzhou was that one of the semi-independent Hebei military governorships was forced back under central control: Wang Du burned himself to death, the Khitan troops were captured, Dingzhou returned to the ordinary prefecture-and-garrison system under an appointed governor, and the appointment of governors and the muster of troops came more firmly into the court's hands, so that for a while no Hebei governor dared openly defy an imperial order. More deeply, the war solved none of the underlying problem. The prefectural soldiers, the elite guards and the garrison farms remained in the governor's hands, and Hebei continued to be the hardest region of the empire to control; that condition was exposed without disguise in 936, when Shi Jingtang ceded the Sixteen Prefectures and called the Khitan south, which shows that the settlement of 928 at Dingzhou was a suppression rather than a cure. For the Khitan the two incursions cost several thousand riders and ended with two thousand taken prisoner, a real price paid for a rescue that achieved nothing, and it made Emperor Taizong Yelü Deguang of Liao more cautious about advancing south, keeping his attention on internal consolidation for a time and thereby altering the rhythm of confrontation between the two northern states over the following decade. For Tang siegecraft, the complete demonstration of siege-by-starvation given by Wang Yanqiu — when the city is strong, surround it and let the grain run out — became a model repeatedly cited in the Five Dynasties and early Song, and is often set beside later Song discussions of attacking the fortified cities of Hebei.
result: 928年四月至929年二月的定州之戰，以唐軍的完全勝利告終。四月二十七日拔北關城，五月在曲陽嘉山擊破王都與禿餒的合兵並奪取西關城，六月強攻失利付出三千餘人代價後改行長圍，七月十九日於唐河再破惕隱七千騎並追至易州；十月明宗遣人督攻城，王晏球不為所動，繼續斷糧困城。929年正月，定州城中糧盡，王都與禿餒突圍不成；二月十三日，定州指揮使馬讓能開城門引唐軍入城，王都在城內自焚，禿餒及二千契丹人被俘，契丹兩次入塞的解圍企圖全部落空。此役之後，義武軍節度使由朝廷重新除派，河北的藩鎮軍力被壓制數年；唐軍取勝的關鍵不在一場硬碰硬的攻城，而在守城方內部斷糧、政府反覆催促強攻而主帥堅持不動，以及最後從內部打開城門。定州城本身在經歷北關、西關兩度失守與圍城近十個月之後被朝廷收復，兩軍在河北平原上的第一次大規模接戰，亦以唐軍完整保有河北主要州城的姿態收場。
resultEn: The War of Dingzhou, from the fourth month of 928 to the second month of 929, ended in a complete Tang victory. The northern barrier fort fell on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month; in the fifth month the combined host of Wang Du and Tu Nei was broken at Jiashan east of Quyang and the western barrier was taken; the forced assault of the sixth month cost three thousand men and was followed by a switch to a long blockade; on the nineteenth day of the seventh month Tiyin's seven thousand riders were beaten on the Tang river and pursued to Yizhou; and when the emperor sent men in the tenth month to demand an assault, Wang Yanqiu did not move, but kept the grain road closed and the city starved. In the first month of 929 the grain in Dingzhou was gone and the attempt of Wang Du and Tu Nei to break out failed; on the thirteenth day of the second month the Dingzhou command officer Ma Rangneng opened the gates to the Tang army, Wang Du burned himself to death inside the city, and Tu Nei with two thousand Khitan were taken prisoner, so that both Khitan attempts to relieve the siege ended in nothing. In its aftermath a new military governor was appointed to Yiwu by the court, and the military power of the Hebei governors was suppressed for several years. What decided the Tang victory was not a storm of the walls but the starvation of the defenders, the refusal of a commander to be hurried into an assault by repeated pressure from his own court, and finally a gate opened from within. Dingzhou itself, having lost both the northern and the western barriers and endured nearly ten months of blockade, was recovered by the court, and the first large engagement between the two armies on the Hebei plain closed with the Tang army still holding the principal cities of the north.
